audits.secondSweep: A dedicated P5/P6 sweep re-read every sentence for inanimate or abstract subjects with agency verbs, roads or geography with motion verbs, receiver nouns with the actor demoted, body-part subjects, and states settling into the body. Roads ('climbed', 'went over the shoulder', 'came out from between the last two barns', 'brings you to the market gate') take literal route verbs. The weight/drag clauses (L3, L13, L249, L309, L311, L349) describe the chapter's magical-sensing mechanism and pass the subject-matter defense. The plague-as-subject clauses ('made to keep and made to wait' L19, 'built there meal after meal and waited' L27, 'it keeps in them and waits' L35, 'ran on flour and finished on its own' L65) describe the designed latency that this chapter is built to reveal (plan: 'ingestion, repeated exposure and body participation as a design'), so the subject-matter defense applies. Body-part subjects (stomach turned over L61, left hand had shut hard L61, chest loosened L163, face went hot L213, teeth began to chatter L311) are all involuntary physiology, the Pattern 8 exception. No Pattern 11 permission tags: 'she let go' at L329 is a literal release of her hand. No Pattern 4 institutional self-deception: the factors/guild/town at L263 are named groups of people in the clerk's dialogue.
audits.cleanReason: 22 candidates were examined across both sweeps. Every grammatical non-person subject with an active verb is one of three things: literal physics or route geography (keep condition 3); a collective with its people visible ('the camp shouting round them' with the shouting men listed next, 'the carts ... took turns' with drivers established at L247 and L277, wagons 'waiting its turn'); or the chapter's literal subject, the designed plague and Jaina's sensing of it, which the subject-matter defense covers. The one non-body subject with a near-volitional sense, 'The old voice came out before she had decided on any voice at all' (L131), stays as an involuntary slip, and that involuntariness is the point of the sentence. See the scratchpad.
